newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil activity slack, low sulphur pressured.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil activity slack, low sulphur pressured.

text.p: NWE cracked fuel oil found little support on Wednesday. Crude softened and physical demand was very sparse.
Dealers said barge activity was significantly poorer today compared with the beginning of the week and most felt that large volumes would not be done until after the Christmas break.
Deals were concluded around $117-$118 a tonne fob ARA with the market ranging during the course of the day between $115-118.50. Supplies in Rotterdam were understood to be good.
"It is very hard to find storage, Rotterdam is pretty much full up," said one dealer at a major.
High sulphur cargoes were also under poor buying pressure.

"With barges off and crude drifting down, there's little reason to pay more than about $115 cif NWE," said one trader. End-users appeared to be covered and prices were not low enough to prompt speculative buying.

The low sulphur market continued to look weak. A 25-27,000 tonne UK cargo was sold early at $126.75 fob NWE. The material is expected to go into the Med. At least four cargoes, one of 45-50,000 tonnes, remain available for Dec and early Jan. Another 45-50kt Jan cargo is likely to join this group.
